title: Karate: Gherkin scenarios without writing glue code

videos.script: Lesson 7 wrote API tests in Java. Every test was a method, and every check was a call. {{java}} Karate writes the same tests as plain scenarios. Given a path, when the method is get, then the status is 200. {{scenario}} That shape comes from Gherkin, the language of Cucumber. In Cucumber, every step needs a Java method behind it, written by somebody. That code is the glue. {{glue}} Karate needs none, because it already knows what a URL, a header and a status are. {{keywords}} You set up a small Maven project with one Java file in it, and after that you write features. {{project}} You compare whole responses with match, including fields whose value you cannot know in advance. {{match}} You ask for a token once and share it between scenarios. {{reuse}} You run one scenario six times from a table, to test the seat limits. {{outline}} And you read the report Karate writes, where a failed step shows the request and the response that failed it.
